company.name: Tidewell Outdoor
company.summary: You sell outdoor and camping gear online from Gothenburg, Sweden. Your 15 person team runs a Shopify store with about 3,000 products and handles many customer emails about orders, returns, and sizing. Your customers are mainly Swedish and Nordic outdoor shoppers, from casual campers to serious hikers.
company.customers: You sell direct to consumers in Sweden and nearby Nordic countries. Typical buyers are campers, hikers, families, and outdoor hobbyists. A small share may be clubs or local resellers.
tech_signals: Google Analytics or similar web analytics

strategy.executive_summary: Tidewell Outdoor runs a 3,000 product Shopify store from Gothenburg with 15 people and a steady flow of order, return, sizing, and stock questions. Your team already has the core systems in place, but most work still moves through shared inboxes, spreadsheets, and manual checks. We estimate your current AI maturity at 2 out of 5: basic tools are connected, but agents are not yet doing routine work. A focused first program can save about 39 hours per week, roughly 6.5 percent of your team's 600 weekly hours, without changing your storefront or warehouse process. Start with customer service replies and stock reorder checks, then expand into marketing and reporting.

maturity.label: Early automation
maturity.note: You have Shopify, a shared inbox or helpdesk, inventory tools, and analytics. The next step is small agents that draft routine replies, check stock, and prepare reports for human approval.

roadmap.title: Fix the highest volume work in Customer Service and Purchasing
items: Connect helpdesk, Shopify, and carrier tracking to an order status agent.
Set up return and exchange drafting with human approval.
Add sizing and fit answer drafts from product specs.
Build daily reorder and late delivery alerts for Purchasing.
Define approval rules and escalation contacts.

roadmap.title: Add marketing content and leadership reporting
items: Launch product email and social post drafting from your Shopify feed.
Start product description and buying guide drafts with SEO checks.
Build weekly sales, margin, and cashflow summary for the founder.
Train the team on review steps and tone of voice.
Track hours saved and error rates weekly.

roadmap.title: Cover warehouse, IT, and ongoing improvement
items: Add return and damage sorting lists for the warehouse.
Set up Shopify and integration issue triage for IT.
Connect carrier claim logs and stock count exceptions.
Review agents monthly and retire low value ones.
Expand to Nordic language replies where quality holds.

risks.risk: Wrong order or return information sent to customers.
risks.mitigation: Keep human approval before sending, and set clear escalation for delayed or damaged orders.

risks.risk: Product specs and stock data are incomplete.
risks.mitigation: Start with your top 200 SKUs, add missing fields, and review data quality weekly.

risks.risk: The team is busy and skips review steps.
risks.mitigation: Assign owners, keep daily review under 30 minutes, and measure time saved.

risks.risk: Customer data privacy and GDPR concerns.
risks.mitigation: Limit access, use approved tools, keep logs, and avoid putting customer data into public AI tools.

risks.risk: Agent costs or complexity grow without clear return.
risks.mitigation: Start with three agents, review monthly, and cancel any agent that does not show clear hours saved.
